clinician.final_diagnosis: A massive vein of Galen aneurysm with a complex abscess combined with cerebral aqueduct blockage causes mild hydrocephalus, which raises intracranial pressure and compresses the brain's structure, ultimately ending the patient's life.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 12-year-old male presented with convulsions, headache, and high-grade fever. Initial non-contrast CT showed a ring ill-defined lesion in the right brain hemisphere with edema and a hyperdense lesion posterior to the third ventricle compressing the lateral ventricles. Subsequent contrast-enhanced CT and reconstructed images confirmed a 5.7 × 4.7 × 5.3 cm2 right frontal peripherally enhancing cystic brain lesion with huge vasogenic edema, mass effect, and a 1.5 cm midline shift, consistent with a complex brain abscess. Imaging also revealed an avidly enhancing lesion within the third ventricle with extensive vascular loops, consistent with a vein of Galen aneurysm, causing compression of the cerebral aqueduct, leading to mild hydrocephalus and dilation of both lateral ventricles. These findings collectively indicate significantly raised intracranial pressure and compression of brain structures. The patient passed away 2 hours after the scanning procedures.
